display.title: Zaidy Teaches Tov Li Toras Picha: Torah Study and the Maggid's True Home
display.summary_short: A grandfather teaches his grandchildren in Yiddish why Torah learned in this world is dearer to Hashem than Gan Eden, and tells how the Mezritcher Maggid explained his empty house.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish at home, with the children answering and repeating. A grandfather explains the four times in the Shema when we learn Torah: 'when you sit in your house' is the soul in Gan Eden, its true home; 'when you walk on the way' is life in this world, a temporary road; 'when you lie down' is the soul's return after a person's life; and 'when you rise' is Techiyas HaMeisim. He then teaches a maamar of the Alter Rebbe on Dovid HaMelech's words 'Tov li toras picha mei'alfei zahav vachasef': gold and silver stand for the awe and love of Hashem that the soul feels in Gan Eden, and Avraham Avinu called himself 'dust and ashes' beside them, yet the Torah a Jew learns here is dearer still. The children read the text with him line by line. He ends with two stories from Likkutei Dibburim: why the pilgrims returning from the Beis HaMikdash went home 'to their tents', and how a chassid brought a letter from the Baal Shem Tov to the Mezritcher Maggid, found him teaching young children in a broken, empty house, and asked where his furniture was.
display.lesson: Every bit of Torah a child learns in this world is more precious to Hashem than the delights of Gan Eden; this world is only a road, and our true home is built by our mitzvos.
